name: Eusebius of Caesarea
knownFor: Bishop of Caesarea in Palestine who wrote the first history of the church and a Life of Constantine.

keyWorks.title: Church History
keyWorks.about: the church from Christ to his own day, built from the documents he could find

keyWorks.title: Life of Constantine
keyWorks.about: the emperor he knew, with the story of the cross of light

traces: He has long been called the Father of Church History. Arthur McGiffert, who translated him, says the title is deserved.
Socrates of Constantinople built his own account of the Council of Nicaea on Eusebius's words.
remembered: Sabinus, bishop of the Macedonians at Heraclea in Thrace, scorned the Council of Nicaea but still called Eusebius a trustworthy witness, Socrates of Constantinople says.

uncertain: Potamo, a bishop from Heraclea in Egypt, charged at Tyre in 335 that Eusebius had escaped prison by some unlawful promise. Epiphanius of Salamis tells it, writing decades later on the side of Athanasius of Alexandria. Arthur McGiffert, who translated Eusebius, notes that Potamo only guessed, and Athanasius says only that Eusebius was "accused of sacrificing."
How far he truly accepted the Nicene wording is argued. His own letter says he accepted it only after asking what it meant. Eustathius of Antioch said he twisted it.
Constantine's vision of the cross rests on what the emperor told Eusebius under oath. Ernest Richardson, who translated the Life of Constantine, notes that the account was doubted from the first.
